items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: And eventually, he did bring it to New York and it was presented to us, and we -- he rehearsed it and taught it to us

ctx.x: And, imagine having something like this happen to someone in my position or the guys, and, well, I flipped out and so did the guys in the band. It was all arranged through a mutual friend who actually became some way or other a music publisher, but not as a publisher but as a song plugger for a publisher. But he was a very astute guy, and he was a former bassist, he'd been in a couple of bands. And somehow, he got to latch on to Mr. Stravinsky and he started to play our records for Mr. Stravinsky. Then I believe…

And eventually, he did bring it to New York and it was presented to us, and we -- he rehearsed it and taught it to us, actually, because we weren't that accomplished, to play pure Stravinsky, because that's what it was. It wasn't jazz, nor was it meant to be. As he put it, the challenge was to write for with such bastard instrumentation, and he did add, -- he said, because he had to add a horn and a harp.
